description:
Hey Innovators! I'm Dilson Joy Pinto from Karnataka, leading a team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Universal Event). I specialize in computer architecture, C, Python, and analytics.

We are building Healthcare Monitoring Software for Astronauts. To beat deep-space communication delays, we're creating an offline AI "digital doctor" to track vitals and predict health risks.

Looking for passionate minds in software dev, AI/ML, UI/UX, or space tech. Let's win this hackathon!
summary:
Aetheris Care is a web-based health monitoring platform designed to help astronauts keep track of their health during space missions. We developed a dashboard where astronauts can enter health information such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep hours and mood, and receive an assessment based on the information provided.

The platform brings these readings together in one place, making it easier to understand an astronaut's current health status, review previous assessments, and notice changes over time through health trends and alerts. It also provides health-related insights to help astronauts become more aware of their well-being.

Maintaining good health in space is challenging because astronauts work in an environment very different from Earth, where regular medical support may not always be immediately available. Aetheris Care aims to make health monitoring more accessible and organized, helping astronauts stay informed about their health throughout a mission.
details:
Aetheris Care is a web-based platform developed to help astronauts monitor and keep track of their health during space missions. The idea behind our project is simple: astronauts should be able to record their health information, understand their current condition and review changes over time without having to go through scattered records.

The platform allows users to enter important health details such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep duration and mood. After submitting the information, the system generates an assessment and displays the results in a dashboard. Users can also view previous health reports, follow health trends and check alerts that may need attention.

One of the main things we wanted to achieve was to bring all these features together in one place instead of making health monitoring complicated. We considered the challenges of living and working in space, the importance of regular health checks and the need for a simple interface that is easy to understand.

We developed the frontend using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP and Bootstrap. For the backend, we used Python with Flask to handle requests and process health information, while SQLite is used for storing records. The project is a software-based prototype and does not require additional hardware.

What makes Aetheris Care meaningful to us is its focus on both present health information and previous records. We wanted to create something that could help astronauts become more aware of their well-being during missions, especially when immediate medical support may not always be available. Our aim is to make health information easier to access, understand and monitor. Aetheris Care is a prototype for health monitoring and awareness, not a replacement for professional medical advice or diagnosis.
